transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I’m having a hard time staying on track. Like, I’ll be working on a dashboard, and then one Slack ping or even a song lyric or a random idea for another project pulls me away, and suddenly I’ve completely lost what I was doing. It’s been frustrating.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety?

Yeah, pretty often. In meetings or portfolio reviews I’ll be bouncing my leg, clicking a pen, twisting my rings, or just shifting around in my chair. I usually don’t even notice I’m doing it until someone looks at me.
Do you often interrupt others when they're speaking?

Yeah, I do sometimes. Like when people are brainstorming, I’ll blurt out my idea before they’re done explaining theirs. Or I’ll start adding things to their Figma board too quickly. I don’t mean to be rude—I’m usually just excited—but afterward I realize I probably came off as pushy.
Do you often act on impulses when you're alone, like buying something spontaneously or starting a new project without thinking it through?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I’ll sometimes get an idea and want to jump into it, but I haven’t really paid attention to whether I’m doing it without thinking. I don’t know if I’d call it a big issue.
Do you have trouble waiting for your turn in line or in other situations?

Yeah, I do sometimes. Like during hackathon check-ins or waiting in office-hour lines, I get really antsy. I’ll keep checking the time, shifting around, and I kind of have to stop myself from wanting to jump in before it’s actually my turn.
Do you have trouble organizing tasks and managing your time?

I’m not totally sure. I mean, I use calendars and reminders a lot, so I can usually keep things together, but I don’t really know if I’m worse at it than other people. I haven’t paid super close attention to that specifically.
Do you have trouble controlling your emotions when you get frustrated or upset?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I get frustrated sometimes like anyone, but I haven’t noticed myself losing control of my emotions in a big way. I’d probably need to think about it more.
Do you often get easily annoyed or irritable?
I don’t think so, not often. I mean, I can get annoyed sometimes, but I haven’t noticed being especially irritable compared to other people.
Were you more physically active or restless than your peers when you were a child?

Yeah, I think so, at least from what I’ve been told. In elementary school, teachers would write comments about me rushing through worksheets, forgetting the directions, or talking over other kids during group work. And at home, my parents had to sit with me during homework because I’d get up, wander off, or start doing something else before I finished.
Have you experienced these symptoms of restlessness and difficulty staying on track for as long as you can remember, even as a teenager?

Yeah, I think it’s been there for as long as I can remember. Like even in elementary school, teachers would write that I rushed through worksheets, lost track of the directions, or talked over classmates during group work. And at home my parents would sit next to me during homework because I’d wander off or start something else before finishing.
Do you have difficulty following through on instructions or finishing tasks at work or at home?

Yes, sometimes. If someone gives me a list of changes or revisions to do, I’ll usually do the first couple right away, but then I kind of drift into tweaking or redesigning something else. Then I’ll realize later I left one small but important change unfinished.
Do you have trouble focusing or making mistakes in your work or daily activities due to not paying attention to details?

Yes, I do. I’ll think something is finished, like a mockup or a data chart, and then later I’ll notice I mislabeled an axis or used the wrong color key. Sometimes it’s just one tiny instruction in the brief that I somehow missed, even though I thought I’d checked it.
Do you still find yourself being more physically active or restless than your peers now that you're an adult?

Yeah, I do still feel restless. Like if I’m on a long Zoom call or I have to sit and work quietly in one spot for a while, I start getting this uncomfortable feeling in my body, like I need to get up and pace or at least do something with my hands.
Have these difficulties with restlessness, staying on track, and finishing tasks caused significant problems in your relationships or work performance?

Yes. It’s not like my whole life is falling apart, but it has caused problems. I’ve lost a couple small freelance contracts because I didn’t follow through cleanly, and I missed out on a portfolio competition for the same kind of reason. Some friends and collaborators are also more hesitant to work with me now, even though they like my ideas, because they’re not sure I’ll finish things reliably.
Do you feel like these difficulties are causing you a lot of distress or discomfort?

Yeah, it does bother me. I feel embarrassed and frustrated because I’ve lost small freelance contracts and missed out on a portfolio competition when people couldn’t count on me to follow through cleanly. And it’s hard knowing some friends or collaborators still like my ideas, but hesitate to work with me because they’re not sure I’ll finish things reliably.
Did you have difficulty controlling your behavior or waiting for your turn in games when you were a child?

Yeah, waiting my turn has been hard for me. Like in hackathon check-ins or office-hour queues, I get really antsy. I’ll keep checking the time, shifting around, and I have this urge to jump in before it’s actually my turn.
Have you experienced these difficulties with restlessness and staying on track in multiple areas of your life, such as at work, at home, and in social situations?

I’m not totally sure how to separate it out. I’ve noticed it in situations where I’m supposed to stay focused or wait, but I don’t know if I can clearly say it happens in every area like work, home, and social stuff.
Do you experience these difficulties with restlessness and staying on track at home, when you're not working?

Yeah, at home too. On days when I don’t have classes or any real schedule, I still end up bouncing between things—like editing a prototype, then cleaning my desk, then opening some new dataset. It’s like just resting feels kind of weird unless I’m actively doing something.
Do you think your difficulties with staying on track and finishing tasks are mainly because you have trouble paying attention or because you get distracted by other things you want to do?

I think it’s mostly that I get distracted by other things. Like I’ll be working on a dashboard, and then one Slack ping, or even a song lyric, or some random idea for another project pops up, and I lose the thread of what I was doing. Then it takes me a while to get back to it, if I do.
Do you often find yourself making careless mistakes or overlooking details in your work or daily activities?

Yeah, I do. I’ll think something is finished, like a mockup or a data chart, and then later I’ll notice I mislabeled an axis or used the wrong color key. Sometimes it’s something small in the instructions too, like I missed one little part of the brief even though I thought I read it.
